finalText:
Five files, one small HTTP service. Here's how they connect:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  server.js -- checks token via --> auth.js
  server.js -- valid request --> routes.js
  routes.js -- reads --> cache.js
  cache.js -- miss --> store.js
  routes.js -- writes --> store.js
```

- **`server.js`** — the front door. Checks the `Authorization` header, rejects with 401 if bad, otherwise hands the request to the router.
- **`auth.js`** — makes and checks bearer tokens shaped `userId.signature`, signed with a shared secret from `AUTH_SECRET`.
- **`routes.js`** — the route table. `GET /users` and `GET /orders` read through the cache; `POST /orders` writes straight to the store.
- **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of reads. No expiry of its own.
- **`store.js`** — the data itself, kept in memory, each record dying 15 minutes after it's written.

One thing worth knowing before you touch orders: the comment in `routes.js` says writes invalidate the cache, but `POST /orders` never actually clears the `orders:<userId>` cache entry. So a user can add an order and still get the old list back from cache until it falls out of the LRU. Worth checking if that's a known gap or news to you.
